proposal.hypothesis: On SM 8.0+, decomposing each signed 64-bit lane value into four 16-bit limbs permits four native 32-bit warp reductions instead of repeated 64-bit shuffle stages. Each limb sum over 32 lanes fits in int; valid intermediate totals remain within signed 64-bit bounds. The limb extraction and reconstruction may offset any instruction savings, so a full-call speedup is not assumed. Older architectures retain the existing 64-bit shuffle path.

retained: Add an SM 8.0+ warp reduction that decomposes signed 64-bit lane values into four 16-bit limbs, reduces each limb with the existing int warp reduction, and reconstructs the exact lane-zero sum.

Use the new helper for both per-warp reduction stages; retain the pre-SM 8.0 64-bit shuffle fallback, four shared warp partials, single CTA barrier, recursive global passes, 128-thread mapping, and one input per lane.
